license_note: Drill diameters are dimensional facts defined by public standards (ASME B94.11M-1993 for the fractional, number and letter series; ISO 235 / DIN 338 / DIN 345 diameter lists for the metric series). Numeric values are not copyrightable; the standards documents themselves are owned by ASME, ISO and DIN. Jobber lengths are from the DIN 338 length table (recall). h8 deviations are ISO 286-2. Compiled by PartForge from the standards' published values; the metric list is the stocked catalogue series, NOT a Renard R'40 series (earlier versions of this table claimed that; the claim was wrong for about half the rows and has been removed).

columns.key: unique row id. NOT the join key for other tables -- join on 'name'.
columns.name: drill designation as marked on the shank (fraction in inches, #number, letter, or 'x.x mm'). This is the JOIN KEY that fasteners_un / fasteners_metric / npt tables use (their us_tap_drill / tap_drill / clearance_* designation fields).
columns.in: nominal diameter, decimal inches, as a JSON number (trailing zeros lost). Fraction: exact fraction rounded to 4 places HALF-TO-EVEN (the ASME printed value: 1/64 -> 0.0156, 5/32 -> 0.1562). Number: ASME 4-place value. Letter: ASME 3-place value. Metric: mm/25.4 rounded to 4 places half-to-even (derived). Do NOT value-join on this column: fasteners_un/npt store the exact fraction (0.421875) where this stores 0.4219; use 'in_exact' or 'name'.
columns.in_text: the inch value as printed text with the standard's decimal places preserved ('0.0160', '0.1250', '0.234'). Use this for display; never format 'in' with fewer places.
columns.in_exact: exact inch value (fraction evaluated exactly, e.g. 27/64 = 0.421875) for value-joins with fasteners_un / npt, which store the exact fraction. For number/letter rows equals 'in'; for metric rows equals mm/25.4 unrounded.
columns.mm: nominal diameter, millimetres, 3 places as a JSON number. Metric: the standard's nominal (exact by construction). Inch series: EXACT inch value x 25.4 rounded to 3 places HALF-TO-EVEN. Two fractional rows are exact ties (3/16 = 4.7625 -> 4.762, 7/16 = 11.1125 -> 11.112); half-to-even matches the ASME B94.11M / Machinery's Handbook printed metric column; round-half-up (Excel, JS Math.round) gives 4.763 / 11.113. Any script that regenerates this column must use half-to-even (Python round() / decimal ROUND_HALF_EVEN) or it will silently flip those two rows.
columns.mm_text: the mm value as 3-place text ('6.350', '12.700') for display.
columns.din338_jobber_oal_mm: overall length of a DIN 338 (ISO 235 jobber-series) drill of this diameter, mm, from the DIN 338 length table by diameter range. RECALL. Applies to the diameter regardless of series; ASME B94.11M jobber lengths for inch drills are similar but not identical. null below 1 mm and above 20 mm.
columns.din338_jobber_flute_mm: flute (cutting) length of a DIN 338 jobber drill of this diameter, mm. RECALL. Maximum practical full-diameter hole depth with a jobber drill is somewhat less than this; above about 4xD peck-drill, above about 6xD use a long-series (DIN 340) or aircraft-extension drill.
columns.iso_h8_lower_dev_mm: lower deviation of ISO 286 tolerance class h8 for this diameter (upper deviation 0), mm. ISO 235 / DIN 338 drills are made to h8 on diameter (likely). A drill can therefore be up to this much UNDER nominal, and never over; add to the cutting-oversize allowance in notes. Not the ASME B94.11M tolerance, which is a separate +0/-x table not reproduced here.
columns.nearest_alt_name: name of the closest drill in the OTHER measurement system (for a metric row: nearest fraction/number/letter drill; for an inch row: nearest metric drill), by arithmetic over this table.
columns.nearest_alt_delta_mm: nearest_alt diameter minus this diameter, mm, signed (positive = the alternative is larger). Substitution must still be checked against the thread / clearance table: e.g. 3.3 mm (M4 tap) -> #30 is -0.036 mm, too small for a 75% M4 thread in aluminium.
columns.confidence: certain | likely | recall -- for the row's diameter values ('in','mm'). Per-field confidence for the derived columns is in field_confidence.
columns.field_confidence: object: per-field confidence for columns whose confidence differs from the row's.
columns.disputed: present only on rows where reviewers disagreed on a value: lists the kept value, the alternatives and why.
columns.added_reason: present only on rows added during reconciliation: why the size was added.

notes: JOIN KEY: other PartForge tables (fasteners_un, fasteners_metric, npt) refer to drills by designation; join on 'name' (e.g. '#7', 'F', '27/64', '4.2 mm'), never on 'in' (this table stores 4-place rounded values, they store exact fractions) and never on 'mm' for 3/16 and 7/16 (rounding-tie rows; fasteners_metric.final and npt.final store 11.113 for 7/16, this table stores the ASME-printed 11.112). 'in_exact' is provided for value-joins. ROUNDING: 'in' for fractions and 'mm' for all inch-series rows are rounded HALF-TO-EVEN to match the ASME printed values (1/64 = 0.015625 -> 0.0156; 3/16 = 4.7625 mm -> 4.762; 7/16 = 11.1125 mm -> 11.112). Regenerate only with a half-to-even rounding (Python round / decimal ROUND_HALF_EVEN); Excel ROUND and JS Math.round are half-up and will flip 3/16 and 7/16 to 4.763 / 11.113. 'in' and 'mm' are JSON numbers and lose trailing zeros (0.016 not 0.0160); use 'in_text' / 'mm_text' for display so a machinist reading the UI sees the standard's places. ALL VALUES ARE NOMINAL DRILL DIAMETERS. A twist drill cuts oversize: rule of thumb +0.02 to +0.13 mm (0.001-0.005 in) on a hand-fed or unreamed hole in aluminium, more if the drill is dull, mis-ground or the setup lacks rigidity (RECALL; Machinery's Handbook 'Accuracy of Drilled Holes' gives measured oversize data of this order; treat as guidance, not a spec). The drill itself is toleranced UNDER nominal (ISO h8, see iso_h8_lower_dev_mm), so the as-drilled hole is typically nominal minus a few microns plus the cutting oversize. Do not use these diameters as the as-machined hole size for a press fit, a dowel, an O-ring gland bore or any pressure-bearing feature: drill undersize and ream or bore to size. DOWEL / REAMER PREP (recall, common shop practice, verify against the reamer maker's chart): 1/8 dowel: drill #31 (0.1200) then ream 0.1250; 3/16 dowel: #13 (0.1850) then ream 0.1875; 1/4 dowel: #1 (0.2280) then ream 0.2500; 3 mm dowel: 2.9 mm then ream 3 H7; 4 mm: 3.8 mm then 4 H7; 5 mm: 4.8 mm then 5 H7; 6 mm: 5.8 mm then 6 H7; 8 mm: 7.8 mm then 8 H7; 10 mm: 9.8 mm then 10 H7. Reamer allowance ~0.1-0.2 mm on diameter for 3-10 mm, ~0.005-0.010 in for 1/8-1/4 in. TAP AND CLEARANCE DRILLS: this table is a diameter lookup only. The authoritative tap-drill and clearance-drill assignments are fasteners_un.final.json (UN threads: tap_drill_75/50, clearance_close/normal/loose), fasteners_metric.final.json (ISO metric: tap_drill_mm = d - p, tap_drill_stainless_mm, sti_insert_drill_mm, clearance_fine/medium/coarse per ISO 273) and npt.final.json (NPT: tap_drill, tap_drill_reamed). Every drill those tables name now has a row here: the reconciliation added the metric sizes they reference that the original 0.1/0.2/0.5 mm stepping skipped (2.05, 3.1, 3.3, 4.3, 4.5, 5.3, 5.5, 6.3, 6.4, 6.6, 6.8, 8.3, 8.4, 10.2, 10.4, 13.5-19.5 by 0.5, 20.5-24, and the stainless/NPT-nearest sizes) and extended the fractional series past 1/2 in to 1-1/4 in by 1/64 (33/64, 17/32, 35/64, 39/64, 11/16, 55/64 for bolt clearance; 37/64, 23/32, 45/64, 29/32, 59/64, 1-9/64, 1-5/32 for NPT). Common overlaps: 1/4 = E = 6.350 mm; #7 (0.2010) is the 1/4-20 75% tap drill; F (0.2570) is the 5/16-18 tap drill; 5/16 = 7.938 mm; 3/8 = 9.525 mm; 1/2 = 12.700 mm; M6 tap drill is 5.0 mm (not 5.1); M5 tap drill 4.2 mm and M10 tap drill 8.5 mm are in the table. METRIC SERIES PROVENANCE: the metric rows are the stocked DIN 338 / ISO 235 catalogue series (0.1 mm steps to 13 mm, 0.5 mm steps 13-20 mm, plus the 0.05 mm and 0.25 mm step sizes and >20 mm sizes added for sibling-table joins). They are NOT the Renard R'40 preferred numbers (R'40 near these sizes runs 2.24, 2.36, 2.65, 3.15, 3.35, 3.55, 4.25, 4.75, 5.3, 5.6, 6.3, 6.7, 7.1 ...); an earlier version of this table mis-cited 'R'40 per ISO 3294' and that citation is withdrawn. Whether 'ISO 3294' is the correct number of the twist-drill diameter-range standard is unverified; ISO 235 and DIN 338 are the cited documents. CONFIDENCE: #80-#60 are 'likely' rather than 'certain' because that region is spaced in 0.001-0.002 in increments that are easy to transpose; three independent reviewers reproduced all 21 values, so they are believed correct, but the label is kept honest. #59-#1 and A-Z are fixed lookups from ASME B94.11M, 'certain'. Fractional rows over 1 in and metric rows added during reconciliation are 'likely' or 'recall' on the question of whether the size is a catalogue-listed standard size; the diameter number itself is exact by arithmetic/construction in every case. Rows 14.3 mm and 17.9 mm (fasteners_metric stainless tap drills for M16/M20) and 14.75 / 18.25 mm (npt nearest-metric) are 'recall' on availability: verify a vendor stocks them before designing around them. NOT IN THIS TABLE: ASME B94.11M jobber lengths and the ASME diameter tolerance table for inch drills (DIN 338 lengths are given as a proxy, recall); screw-machine (stub) and long-series lengths; drills above 1-1/4 in or 29.5 mm; 0.05 mm step sizes other than 1.65 and 2.05; the 0.01-0.02 mm step micro sizes below 1 mm in DIN 338. Rows dropped during reconciliation: none (no reviewer found any diameter too uncertain to cut metal from).
